candidates.title: Riyadh Season: BLVD City
candidates.summary: Boulevard City is one of Riyadh Season’s most iconic entertainment hubs, offering a vibrant mix of attractions, from the dazzling dancing fountain to upscale dining, shopping, theaters, and immersive experiences for all ages. Visitors can explore OLULOU, where a towering dinosaur skeleton offers the perfect photo op, and let kids dive into four imaginative zones at PLAY-TOPIA. For thrill-seekers, Poppy Playtime delivers suspense inside an abandoned toy factory, A Lot Like Life challenges your bravery in a zombie outbreak, and The Conjuring opens October 15 with spine-chilling scenes from the haunted universe of Annabelle. Families can brave the haunted farm at Zeela House, while pop culture lovers enjoy FUNKO (from Nov 15), with giant figures and collectibles, and gamers embark on a real-world adventure inside MINECRAFT (also from Nov 15). Launching December 18, Flying Over Saudi offers a groundbreaking 5D flight experience that takes you on a 7-minute immersive ride above Saudi Arabia’s most iconic landmarks.

candidates.title: Horses and Equestrian Heritage Exhibition
candidates.venue: King Abdulaziz Public Library (Khurais Branch), Riyadh
candidates.summary: The King Abdulaziz Public Library is hosting a specialized exhibition on horses and equestrian heritage in celebration of Saudi Founding Day. The exhibition showcases a rich collection of manuscripts, rare books, photographs, historical documents, Islamic miniatures, and illustrated works highlighting the deep-rooted equestrian legacy of the Kingdom. Marking four decades of preserving cultural heritage, the library also presents selections from its dedicated Equestrian Center, which houses more than 12,000 rare Arabic and international references on horses, alongside historic photographs captured by Princess Alice of Britain during her 1938 visit to Saudi Arabia.

candidates.title: Solo Art Exhibition Series

candidates.summary: Misk Art Institute presents the third edition of the Solo Series, spotlighting established Saudi artists Fouad Mougharbel and Saad Almasari, whose work has contributed significantly to the Kingdom’s evolving visual culture. candidates.rich_summary: Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Global Positioning System’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by Indranjan Banerjee and Lucas Morin. Global Positioning System is an exhibition dedicated to mapping and navigation systems. It tells stories of fast cars and slow trains, street barriers and trembling grounds, warping highways and broken bridges. Gathering over forty artists across Art Jameel’s two centres in Jeddah and Dubai, the exhibition presents a wide range of artistic practices—from research-based engagements with infrastructure projects to conceptual works that question the very perception of distance. Maps, remaining the dominant representation space, carry a heavy weight. Far from reflecting geography objectively, they are instruments of power that embody specific worldviews. Though based on mapping, navigation systems like GPS render traditional maps redundant; they reduce navigation to an abstract exercise and remove the need to comprehend the physical space one moves through.

candidates.title: Registration for International Research Competition on Non-Terrestrial Networks
candidates.summary: The Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST), in partnership with the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), is organizing the 3rd International Research Competition on Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) 2026. candidates.rich_summary: This intensive three-day course with artist and designer Pharah Al-Ghalib offers a comprehensive introduction to wheel-thrown pottery, guiding participants through the full spectrum of the ceramic process. Day 1 Clay & Wheel Fundamentals: Focuses on understanding clay—its qualities, preparation, and potential. Participants will learn wedging techniques before moving to the wheel to practice centering, opening, and pulling walls, creating several forms to be set aside to dry to a leather-hard stage. Day 2 Refinement & Practice: Focuses on refining technique through trimming leather-hard pieces on the wheel, shaping and finishing forms while improving both skill and confidence. Participants will also continue throwing practice, reinforcing foundational techniques and experimenting with new forms. Day 3 Surface Design & Glaze: Explores surface design on unfired clay.

candidates.title: Tafasahu: Make Room
candidates.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra
candidates.summary: Tafasahu: Make Room is an exhibition that showcases a commissioned installation by Saudi architect and artist, Nada AlMulla, which invites you to enter as a guest—to pause, gather and reflect on the conditions of belonging within the context of the traditional Majlis, Arabic for "gathering space." Beyond being a place to receive and host guests, the Majlis has been a vessel for the transmission of knowledge and heritage. The installation deconstructs this space into its essential elements while centering stories, memories and subtle traces of everyday life that animated it: conversations shared over coffee, the lingering scent of incense, the rhythms of gathering and departure. candidates.organizer: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture / Ithra
candidates.summary: Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. candidates.rich_summary: Godus Bros Retrospective at Hayy Cinema Five years after its original release, Shams Al-Ma’arif (2020) by the locally beloved filmmaking duo Godus Bros returns to the big screen! This time, in a never-before-seen Director’s Cut exclusively at Hayy Cinema with the filmmakers presence in this retrospective weekend with films, masterclasses, giveaways, and exclusive chances to meet the cast and crew! The Godus Bros , the filmmaking duo of brothers Sohayb and Faris Godus , began as a YouTube channel that quickly gained popularity among Saudi youth in 2010 and onwards. From short films to creative content, they paved the way for a new generation of Saudi storytellers, offering a bold and authentic local voice. With feature films like Shams Al-Ma’arif (2020) and Ahlam Al-Asr (2024) , they cemented their place in the Saudi filmmaking scene. You know it’s a Godus Bros production the moment it starts; humorous, authentic, and deeply engaged with the local audience.

candidates.title: Jameel Library | Open Call: The Task of the Translator with Sarasija Subramanian
candidates.summary: In the essay The Task of the Translator , Walter Benjamin writes of how there was a singular, “pure” language in the beginning, likened to a flower vase. When this vase broke, its shards became each of the languages we speak today. If this metaphor is considered in the context of translation, then two pieces inherently cannot be identical; they are instead meant to be complementary—matching at an edge, fitting together perfectly, but never the same.
candidates.image_alt: Jameel Library | Open Call: The Task of the Translator with Sarasija Subramanian
candidates.rich_summary: In the essay The Task of the Translator , Walter Benjamin writes of how there was a singular, “pure” language in the beginning, likened to a flower vase. When this vase broke, its shards became each of the languages we speak today. If this metaphor is considered in the context of translation, then two pieces inherently cannot be identical; they are instead meant to be complementary—matching at an edge, fitting together perfectly, but never the same. The Jameel Library invites you to a week-long research lab developed and facilitated by Sarasija Subramanian. It will focus on unpacking translation as both tool and process, particularly on the fantasy of equivalence in translated material—assumptions based on the fact that nothing is lost (or gained, for that matter) during the process. Participants will engage with the possibilities of translation—more specifically the relationship between translation and accessibility—as a way to watch, listen to, and read material closely.

candidates.title: Merath – Middle East Museums & Heritage Expo
candidates.summary: Taking place at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Convention Center, Merath – Middle East Museums & Heritage Expo is the Kingdom’s first dedicated trade event for museums, heritage, and cultural development. The three-day exhibition brings together more than 100 exhibiting companies and over 3,000 visitors, including museums, galleries, science centers, cultural institutions, government entities, private collectors, and heritage developers. Co-located with the Saudi Entertainment and Amusement Expo (SEA Expo) and the Saudi Light and Sound Expo (SLS Expo), Merath provides a strategic platform to connect with decision-makers and explore opportunities within Saudi Arabia’s rapidly expanding $67 billion heritage and museum market, reinforcing Riyadh’s role as a growing hub for cultural innovation and investment.

candidates.title: World Stadiums and Arenas Summit
candidates.summary: The World Stadiums and Arenas Summit—the region’s largest stadiums and sports facilities conference and exhibition—returns to Riyadh at Hilton Riyadh Hotel & Residences. This flagship gathering brings together global leaders, architects, developers, government stakeholders, and sports federations to showcase cutting-edge technologies, sustainable design solutions, and best practices in building and upgrading stadiums and sports venues. With Saudi Vision 2030 driving major investment in sports and entertainment infrastructure, the summit offers a front-row view of the latest industry trends—from smart stadiums to eco-friendly facilities—and how they are shaping the future of sport in the Kingdom and beyond. Register Now World Sports 360 Summit | Athlete 360 Co-located with the World Stadiums and Arenas Summit, World Sports 360 Summit | Athlete 360, brings together global experts, elite athletes, coaches, and industry leaders to shape the future of sports, wellness, and human performance in the Kingdom. Focused on integrating performance and health, the programme spotlights cutting-edge performance optimisation (recovery, data-driven training, and advanced technology), holistic athlete development (nutrition, sports medicine, mental resilience, and long-term wellbeing), and the evolving Saudi sports landscape powered by Vision 2030. Expect practical insights, knowledge exchange, and forward-looking discussions spanning the sports economy, club management, revenue strategies, talent development and scouting, and the latest innovations in athlete technology and performance. Register Now The programme also features the World Stadiums and Arenas Awards , celebrating standout achievements in stadium and arena development across 10 categories highlighting innovation, sustainability, and exceptional project delivery—including architectural design for new venues, renovation and modernisation, innovative materials, multi-use design, creative lighting, eco-friendly architecture, community and social impact, safety and security leadership, accessibility and inclusivity initiatives, and the People’s Choice Award for outstanding stadium design.

candidates.title: Saudi Statistics Forum
candidates.summary: The Second Saudi Statistics Forum is a high-level national platform organized by the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) to strengthen cooperation, promote statistical integration, support capacity development, and facilitate knowledge exchange across the Kingdom's statistical ecosystem. Building on the success of its inaugural edition held in April 2025, the second edition will be held under the theme "Towards an Integrated Statistical Ecosystem" on 9 November 2026 in Riyadh, alongside the 6th United Nations World Data Forum 2026. The Forum is expected to bring together Their Highnesses, Excellencies, ministers, representatives of international organizations and statistical offices, local and international experts, decision-makers, and academics. It will feature specialized sessions and an accompanying exhibition with broad participation from local and international organizations. The Forum aims to raise awareness of the role of official statistics in policymaking and national development, strengthen partnerships between national and international statistical entities, and promote knowledge sharing to support a more integrated and sustainable statistical ecosystem. Register Now Initiative: Road to Riyadh (R2R) As part of the preparations for the 6th United Nations World Data Forum 2026, the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT) launched the "Road to Riyadh" program to promote awareness of the Kingdom's role in data and statistics and support knowledge exchange and international collaboration. The initiative featured a series of in-person and virtual sessions, seminars, and workshops held across several cities in the Kingdom throughout the year. The program reflects GASTAT's ongoing efforts to strengthen the Kingdom's position in the statistical field and support the development of data and statistical systems in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and Saudi Vision 2030. Adieu Bonaparte is one of his other feats of strength in the historical genre. In 1798, Napoleon lands his army in Egypt, defeats the Mameluke warlords (the remnants of Ottoman rule), and reaches Cairo. Three brothers, Egyptian patriots, chafe under Mameluke rule and reject the prospect of French domination. Bakr, the eldest, is a hothead, quick to advocate armed rebellion; Ali is more philosophical and poetic while Yehia is young and impressionable.

candidates.image_alt: Hayy Cinema | Youssef Chahine Retrospective: Alexandria, Why? (1979)
candidates.rich_summary: OPENING FILM Alexandria Why / Iskindereya Leh Director: Youssef Chahine Release Date: 1978 Running Time: 120min Language: Arabic Subtitles: English Alexandria, Why? Marked a radical, newly introspective turn in Chahine’s active career, a sharp departure from his Fifties musicals and melodramas and his later epics and political films. The first of a semi-autobiographical tetralogy, entitled “Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man,” Alexandria, Why? focuses on a precocious adolescent whose dreams and colorful attempts to become an actor unfold against the vivid backdrop of Alexandria during World War II. A rich cast inspires Chahine’s young thespian hero with a wealth of dramatic sub-plots – at turns hilarious and touching – about wartime life. The autobiographical nature and nostalgic flavour of Alexandria, Why? make it one of Chahine’s most accessible works, a charming and entertaining film that also delivers a potently subversive and impassioned anti-war message. candidates.title: AlUla Tour
candidates.organizer: Royal Commission for AlUla / Experience AlUla
candidates.summary: AlUla Tour is a major fixture on the international cycling calendar, attracting the world’s top teams and riders for a multi-stage race through one of the most spectacular landscapes on Earth. From dramatic desert backdrops to iconic landmarks like Maraya and the Oasis, each stage delivers high performance and unforgettable scenery in equal measure. Individual AlUla Tour stages will be announced closer to the race date, but previous editions have seen riders traverse routes from Old Town to Harrat Uwayrid and Winter Park to Wirkah Mountain.

candidates.title: Hayy Cinema | Hayy Classics: An Experience from Jeddah's Past
candidates.summary: Hayy Classics: An Experience from Jeddah’s Past Join us at Hayy Cinema for a nostalgic experience of Jeddah’s cinematic and cultural past. Relive the charm of outdoor cinemas as we showcase classic films on a 35mm projector under the stars at Saha. Outdoor cinemas first emerged in Jeddah in the early 1960s, bringing communities together to enjoy a vibrant mix of international and Arab films. In addition to the screenings, join us for related workshops and panel discussions.

candidates.title: 24th ERRA Annual Conference
candidates.summary: The 24th ERRA Annual Conference takes place in Riyadh from February 1 to 3, bringing together international regulators, experts, and industry leaders to discuss the future of electricity sector governance and transformation. Hosted by the Saudi Electricity Regulatory Authority (SERA), the conference is held under the theme “From Oversight to Foresight: The Proactive Regulator in the Electricity Transformation.” The conference explores forward-looking regulatory approaches, innovation in electricity markets, consumer protection, and evolving energy systems. It also reflects Riyadh’s growing role as a destination for major international forums and supports the Kingdom’s wider ambitions in energy leadership and sustainable development. Registration

candidates.rich_summary: Director: Afnan Bawyan Country: Saudi Arabia Year: 2023 Language: Arabic, Urdu, Tigrinya Subtitles: English Sixty-year-old Hajer lives alone in Historic Jeddah. She prepares the famous local rice dish “Saleeg”. She hears the bell of the grocer outside. She hurries to the living room window, and neglects to cover the pot. The birds fly in and begin to nibble, but accidentally knock off the rice into the pot, and it begins to cook and expand in size. While Hajer struggles with the Indian grocer who fails to understand her, Saleeg fills the entire kitchen and overflows into the rest of the house. Hajer panics and grabs a ladle and scoops Saleeg into multiple plates and sets them in the hallway. Someone knocks at the door, her neighbor’s daughter Shams is offering a plate of food, but Shams freaks out at the Saleeg and runs away. Hajer asks her foreign neighbors for help, who do not understand her. Saleeg floods the rest of the house and into the yard, carrying Hajer outside.

candidates.summary: March & April 2026 At Hayy Cinema Join us this March and April at Hayy Cinema in Jeddah for a month of films exploring memory, resilience and solidarity. candidates.rich_summary: March & April 2026 At Hayy Cinema Join us this March and April at Hayy Cinema in Jeddah for a month of films exploring memory, resilience and solidarity. The programme brings together both contemporary and classic cinema, through different genres offering stories that will surely entertain, inspire, and challenge audiences. The lineup include Sirāt (2025) , the Cannes Film Festival jury prize winner, an escalatingly tense road journey through the Moroccan desert, and Roqia (2025) , an Algerian suspenseful narrative exploring memory, faith, and the supernatural across parallel timelines. French film lovers can also enjoy our monthly cinema club, Rendezvous with French Cinema , featuring Little Amélie or the Character of Rain (2025) , a whimsical and poetic tale that captures the charm of youthful storytelling. The month also features a special Italian Film Night , screening Corri uomo corri (Run, Man, Run!) (1968) , a legendary thrilling Western adventure.

candidates.title: Human Capability Initiative Conference
candidates.venue: King Abdulaziz International Conference Center (KAICC), Riyadh
candidates.summary: Under the patronage of His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince, Prime Minister, and Chairman of the Human Capability Development Program (HCDP) Committee, the third edition of the Human Capability Initiative (HCI) Conference—one of the Saudi Vision 2030 Realization Programs—will take place on April 12–13, 2027, at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme “The Human Code.” The conference will focus on three pillars: deep human connection, sound reasoning amid complexity, and value-driven creation to safeguard human contribution and purpose in the age of accelerated technological advancement. HCI 2027 aims to attract more than 15,000 visitors and over 250 local and international speakers, including policymakers, thought leaders, and experts from government, private, nonprofit, and global institutions, providing a platform to exchange best practices and showcase inspiring global success stories. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland will participate as Country of Honor, reflecting the strength of the Saudi-British strategic partnership in advancing human capability development. Building on the success of previous editions—which welcomed over 23,000 visitors, featured 550+ speakers, and announced more than 156 launches and agreements—the conference reinforces the Kingdom’s commitment to investing in human potential as a foundation for sustainable growth and global competitiveness in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030.

candidates.rich_summary: Join us for the screenings of the third edition of “Kef Hayyak?” cohort’s films! “Kef Hayyak?” is a unique documentary filmmaking challenge that invites aspiring filmmakers to capture the essence of their neighborhoods in Jeddah through their own lens—using only their phones. Building on the success of its first two editions, the programme launched an open call for its third edition in December 2025, selecting 13 projects for development based on the quality and originality of their creative proposals. The participants attended an Introduction to Documentary Filmmaking workshop, where they learned about documentary genres, terminology, techniques, and watched a selection of documentary examples. The workshop was led by filmmaker and Hayy Cinema’s Programming Coordinator, Lama Jamjoom. The participants were trained and mentored in the basics of storytelling and documentary filmmaking.
